reference.title: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Back, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull the elbows up and out, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; lighter than for a regular bent-over row (clinical opinion)
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; slower lowering; chest-supported version to remove the low-back demand

cues.text: Feet hip width, knees soft. Hinge at the hips with a flat back until the chest is close to parallel with the floor. Dumbbells hang under the shoulders, palms facing back (toward the legs).
Breathe out and pull the elbows up and out to the sides, wide of the body, like rowing to the chest.
Upper arms about level with the back, elbows bent about 90 degrees; squeeze the backs of the shoulders and the shoulder blades.
Lower under control in about 2 s back to straight arms.
Keep the hinge and the flat back; repeat without standing up between reps.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows tucked in to the ribs
mistakes.fix: That is a regular row (more lats). Keep the elbows out wide, about 60-90 degrees from the body.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back or standing up as you pull
mistakes.fix: Hold the hinge still; use a lighter weight.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
mistakes.fix: Keep the neck long and pull the elbows out, not up to the ears.
Pause at the bottom and lift with the shoulders only.

kinematics.norm: Hip hinge with the trunk well forward, about 15-30 degrees above horizontal, held still (clinical opinion)
Upper arm about 60-90 degrees out from the trunk so the pull is a horizontal abduction; horizontal abduction loads the posterior deltoid more than a close row (Franke 2015)
Nearly straight at the bottom, about 90 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Pronated (palms back) is the usual rear delt row grip; on a reverse fly a neutral grip gave more posterior deltoid activity than pronated (Schoenfeld 2013)
Soft knees, about 15-30 degrees, so the hips can hinge (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #037712, Dumbbell Rear Delt Row, video (movement reference)

Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The bent-over position loads the low back; keep the back flat and stop if it rounds or aches.
modify: Low-back discomfort: lie face down on an incline bench (chest-supported rear delt row) or rest the head on a bench.
Shoulder pinch at the top: stop the pull when the upper arms are just short of level with the back.
regressions: Chest-supported rear delt row on an incline bench.
progressions: Bent-over rear delt fly (straighter arms, longer lever).

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: with the elbows out wide the row becomes a horizontal abduction (a bent-arm reverse fly). Horizontal abduction (reverse peck deck) gave much higher posterior deltoid activity than a close-elbow seated row (Franke 2015; Botton 2013).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Prime mover: with the elbows out wide the row becomes a horizontal abduction (a bent-arm reverse fly). Horizontal abduction (reverse peck deck) gave much higher posterior deltoid activity than a close-elbow seated row (Franke 2015; Botton 2013).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Pull the shoulder blades together at the top of the row.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Pull the shoulder blades together at the top of the row.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: External rotator that works with the posterior deltoid in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: External rotator that works with the posterior deltoid in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps hold the upper arm out from the body as it rises.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps hold the upper arm out from the body as it rises.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the elbow bend; less involved than in a close row because the elbows lead.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Holds the elbow bend; less involved than in a close row because the elbows lead.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the flat back in the hinge for the whole set.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the flat back in the hinge for the whole set.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the hips in the hinge.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the hips in the hinge.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk so it does not rock as the arms move.
